Dear Mr. Herried:
We have completed our review of the draft environmental impact statement for the I-94 General Mitchell Field Airport Spur in the City of Milwaukee, Milwaukee County.
It does not appear that any of the five corridors indicated would have a significant effect on fish or wildlife habitat if constructed. As a result, we have no preference for any of the corridors indicated in this regard.
Additional comments concerning air quality considerations from our Bureau of Air Pollution Control and Solid Waste Disposal are attached. Because the Airport Spur will connect the interstate highway system to General Mitchell Field, it will have the effect of committing that airport as Milwaukee's primary air transport facility with its resultant long-term impact on air quality. This commitment is more than a secondary or subtle impact of the proposed freeway and, as such, is discussed in detail in the staff comments attached. While some of the alternatives proposed deal wholly or partly with General Mitchell Field, it should be recognized that the freeway-airport system in part is a larger transportation complex. Although the Division of Highways has taken the lead in preparing the environmental impact statement for the airport spur, the air-land transportation question would be within the purview of the Department of Transportation. It is recommended that the Final Environmental Impact Statement include a comprehensive overview of the total transportation needs being served.
